chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il al-Ash'ari said: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abu Malik al-Juhani said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying

Three people with whom God shall not speak on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at them, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: One who claims a leader whose leadership is not from God; one who denies a leader whose leadership is from God the Exalted; and one who considers that both of them have a share in Islam.
ai.seo_question: Who are the three people God will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the centrality of Imamah in Shia theology by identifying three groups excluded from divine favor: those who follow a non-divine leader, those who deny the divinely appointed Imam, and those who syncretize both. This triad underscores the Shia view that political and spiritual authority must be exclusively rooted in divine designation (Nass), rejecting both rival caliphates and the denial of the Ahl al-Bayt's right. The hadith serves as a theological boundary marker, defining true Islam through adherence to the specific lineage of Imams rather than general communal consensus.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-69 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ali ibn Isma’il al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Abi Malik al-Jihni that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

There are three people with whom God shall not Speak to, Look upon, or Purify on the Resurrection Day. There shall be a great punishment for them. They are those who follow leaders whose leadership is not Divinely Ordained by God; those who deny the leadership of Divine Leaders whose Leadership is Divinely Ordained by God the Honorable the Exalted; and those who consider the previous two groups of people to be Muslims.”
